title: The Potential of Social Identity for Equilibrium Selection

original_source.version_note: Pre-publication author manuscript matching title/authors and central contribution; exact final wording may differ.

central_claims: Salient shared group identity facilitates efficient high-effort coordination in minimum-effort games under the stated parameter conditions.

source_manifest.title: The Potential of Social Identity for Equilibrium Selection

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. Evaluating replicability of laboratory experiments in economics — Supplement, Tables S1–S2
source_manifest.finding: The preregistered independent comparison tests whether enhanced ingroup matching raises effort relative to enhanced outgroup matching; replication N=168, original focal N=72, p=.571. The project only retested one selected result per paper.

source_manifest.title: Best practices in replication: a case study of common information in coordination games
source_manifest.finding: Original authors and Riyanto trace failed replication to common-information procedures; new NUS experiments restore ingroup differences, NTU common-information effect is weaker and pooled result positive.

research.summary: The 2016 focal effect did not replicate (p=.571). Later experiments recover it conditionally on common-information procedures, but original-author involvement and weaker NTU evidence prevent a clean independent-validation judgment.
